title: S3 event notifications and static website hosting
hook: S3 can notify Lambda, SNS, or SQS on object events and serve static sites — pair website hosting with CloudFront for HTTPS production SPAs.

blocks.text: Amazon S3 event notifications fire on s3:ObjectCreated:*, s3:ObjectRemoved:*, and other events to AWS Lambda, Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, or EventBridge. Filters by prefix and suffix. Static website hosting serves index.html and error document from bucket website endpoint — HTTP only; production uses CloudFront. Event delivery is at-least-once.

blocks.text: CSV upload pipelines trigger Lambda ETL. Duplicate events require idempotent handlers. Public website endpoint without CloudFront lacks HTTPS and WAF.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: event notification prefix/suffix filter, async Lambda with DLQ, static site behind CloudFront OAC not public bucket.

diagram.title: S3 event to Lambda
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  User[User upload] --> S3[S3 PutObject uploads/data.csv]

snippet.label: Notification configuration
snippet.explanation: Apply with put-bucket-notification-configuration. One config per bucket replaces previous.

snippet.label: Allow S3 to invoke Lambda
snippet.code:
aws lambda add-permission \
  --function-name ProcessCsv \
  --statement-id s3-invoke \
  --action lambda:InvokeFunction \
  --principal s3.amazonaws.com \
  --source-arn arn:aws:s3:::my-app-data \
  --source-account 123456789012
snippet.explanation: Required before notification succeeds — otherwise configuration errors.

snippet.label: Static website hosting bucket
snippet.code:
WebsiteBucket:
  Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
  Properties:
    WebsiteConfiguration:
      IndexDocument: index.html
      ErrorDocument: error.html
    PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
      BlockPublicAcls: true
      BlockPublicPolicy: true
      IgnorePublicAcls: true
      RestrictPublicBuckets: true
snippet.explanation: Website config without public access — serve via CloudFront OAC instead of public policy.

snippet.label: Put notification from CLI
snippet.explanation: Test with sample upload to prefix and watch CloudWatch Logs for Lambda.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Missing Lambda permission for S3 invoke. Assuming exactly-once S3 events. Public website bucket for production SPA without CloudFront HTTPS.

blocks.text: EventBridge replaces multiple notification configs with central routing and replay. SQS buffer between S3 and Lambda smooths bursts. How to prove it in production: Lambda Errors metric, DLQ depth, duplicate processing rate via idempotency table.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Invalidation or versioned assets on deploy

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Public S3 website for prod React app gets rejected. Strong answer: CloudFront OAC, event-driven idempotent Lambda, DLQ.

interviewTakeaways: S3 events are at-least-once — idempotent Lambda handlers required.
Configure prefix/suffix filters to reduce noise and cost.
Static website hosting is HTTP — use CloudFront OAC for production HTTPS.
60s: ObjectCreated to Lambda with filter. Add permission. Idempotent handler. CloudFront for static site.
commonPitfalls: Exactly-once assumption from S3 events — rejected.
Strong answer: idempotent on key+etag; DLQ for failures.
Forgot lambda add-permission for S3 principal.
No DLQ on async Lambda processing uploads.
